$comment: THE `hello` CONTRACT, asserted from both ends.
`hello` is the only message that carries a whole room, and four of the
things a template promises ride on it: the parts, the panels, the camera
(view.home) and the instruments (view.scopes) — plus whether the room has
a goal at all (machine). Two of those once went missing for a release,
because the server wrote `view` and `machine` beside `room` while the
client forwarded `room` alone as its RoomHello. Both halves compiled. The
TypeScript interface declared the fields it never received.
So the shape lives HERE, in one file neither half owns, and both assert
against it:
server  crates/server/src/lifecycle_tests.rs ::
the_hello_a_room_sends_is_the_shape_the_client_parses
— builds a real hoist room, calls hello_msg, and checks every
path below against the message that goes out on the socket.
client  packages/app/src/wirecheck.ts (pnpm --filter @ee/app wirecheck)
— runs `sample` through net.ts's parseHello, AND feeds it to a
real connect() over a stub socket, checking the object that
reaches onHello. The second half is the one that would have
caught the original bug: the parser was never wrong, the
line that chose what to pass on was.
Move a field on either side and one of the two fails, naming the path.
`types` are the paths a room-serving server must send, with their JSON
types (dots walk into objects). `sample` is a verbatim hello from a room
made from the built-in `hoist` template: the one that ships a camera, a
scope and a goal, so nothing in the contract is exercised by absence.
